description: The transnational human futures movement gains momentum, demanding a binding global treaty on human-level AI systems and the creation of a UN-level agency to oversee existential risk. It draws support from disillusioned AI researchers, climate activists, and faith groups, framing advanced AI as a test of human maturity. The movement begins to influence parliamentary debates in several EU states, despite minimal institutional backing.

Regional governments and municipal networks continue forming local AI civil defense compacts, pooling incident response, sharing detection models, and running joint cyber drills. These bottom-up efforts operate semi-independently of EU coordination, signaling growing institutional fragmentation but also fostering grassroots resilience innovation in the face of central inaction.
